subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Amniocentesis, Cordocentesis and the Anomaly Scan

steps.tx: Needle sampling of amniotic fluid under ultrasound guidance from fifteen weeks is **amniocentesis**. Fetal cells in the fluid give karyotype, microarray and infection studies. Procedure related miscarriage risk is now quoted around one in three hundred to nine hundred. Results from cultured cells take two weeks, while rapid tests answer the common trisomies in one to three days.
steps.say: Amniocentesis samples fluid from fifteen weeks with a small procedure related loss risk.

steps.tx: Sampling fetal blood from the umbilical cord for diagnosis and transfusion is **cordocentesis**. It checks fetal anaemia, platelets and karyotype rapidly from eighteen weeks. In skilled hands it also delivers intrauterine transfusion to the same site. Loss rates near one percent limit it to cases where the answer changes management before delivery.
steps.say: Cordocentesis samples fetal blood from eighteen weeks and can deliver transfusion.

steps.tx: Twenty weeks is when anatomy becomes a checklist rather than an impression. The **anomaly scan** surveys brain, spine, heart, kidneys, limbs and placenta in a set order, measuring growth as it goes. Most serious structural problems declare themselves to a systematic eye, and soft markers need interpretation against screening results rather than isolation. A structured report from this scan decides referrals for the rest of the pregnancy.
steps.say: The twenty week anomaly scan follows a set anatomical checklist with growth measures. Its structured report decides referrals for the pregnancy.

vis.alt: Ultrasound image from a mid pregnancy anomaly scan surveying fetal anatomy.
vis.caption: A fetal profile and anatomy survey are shown on a twenty week ultrasound scan. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: The detailed structural ultrasound at eighteen to twenty weeks is the **anomaly scan**. It systematically examines brain, heart, spine, abdomen and limbs. Detection varies greatly by organ system and operator experience. Open spina bifida detection exceeds 95 percent, while about a third of small ventricular septal defects are missed.
steps.say: The anomaly scan systematically examines fetal structure at eighteen to twenty weeks.

steps.tx: Soft markers on the anomaly scan modestly shift chromosome risk and are called **soft markers**. Isolated soft markers with negative screening usually need no invasive testing. Multiple markers or structural defects change that advice. An echogenic bowel or a short femur alone shifts risk only slightly and rarely justifies a needle test.
steps.say: Soft markers modestly shift risk, and isolated ones with negative screening need no invasion.

steps.tx: Fetal echocardiography follows when heart risk is raised by family history, diabetes or scan findings, termed **targeted cardiac scanning**. outflow tract views detect most major defects. Delivery planning at a cardiac centre follows significant findings. Views of the outflow tracts lift detection of major heart defects from about a third to over two thirds.
steps.say: Targeted cardiac scanning follows raised heart risk and plans delivery at cardiac centres.

steps.tx: Infection testing on amniotic fluid uses polymerase chain reaction for agents like cytomegalovirus, called **amniotic PCR**. Timing after maternal infection matters because fetal shedding must have begun. Ultrasound signs of fetal infection guide who benefits. Testing too early after maternal infection gives false negatives, so sampling waits at least six to eight weeks.
steps.say: Amniotic PCR tests fetal infection after maternal illness with ultrasound guidance.

steps.tx: The event that seeds later haemolytic disease often passes unnoticed at delivery. **Sensitisation** occurs when fetal RhD positive cells enter an RhD negative mother and teach her immune system to make anti D, usually silently. The first baby escapes; the antibody then targets the next RhD positive pregnancy. Anti D prophylaxis works by clearing fetal cells before that lesson is learned, which is why timing after birth and bleeding events matters.
steps.say: Sensitisation happens when fetal RhD cells immunise an RhD negative mother, endangering later pregnancies. Anti D clears those cells before immunity forms.

vis.alt: Image showing RhD sensitisation as fetal red cells enter the maternal circulation.
vis.caption: Fetal RhD positive cells are shown crossing into the maternal bloodstream at delivery. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Rh negative women receive anti-D after invasive procedures to prevent **sensitisation**. Procedures can push fetal cells into maternal circulation. A Kleihauer test may guide additional dosing after later procedures. Five hundred international units of anti-D is the common post procedure dose after 20 weeks in many protocols.
steps.say: Anti-D after invasive procedures prevents Rh sensitisation from fetal cell leakage.

steps.tx: Choosing between CVS and amniocentesis trades earliness against risk and mosaicism, a **test selection decision**. CVS suits early answers and DNA diagnosis, amniocentesis suits neural tube and later presentations. Counselling individualises the choice. Confined placental mosaicism affects about one percent of CVS results and may need amniocentesis to resolve.
steps.say: Test selection trades CVS earliness against amniocentesis advantages by indication.

steps.tx: After invasive testing, pain, leaking fluid or fever mandates immediate contact, summarised as **post procedure advice**. Most procedures settle uneventfully within a day. Written instructions and a contact number are given to every woman. Rh sensitisation checks and a fetal heart check complete the visit before the woman leaves.
steps.say: Post procedure advice warns about pain, leaking and fever after invasive testing.
